fe.intro:
A direct cremation in Colorado has a median cost of $1,650 and an immediate burial $2,565 — 17% and 8% below the national medians, and cheaper than average on every funeral-home charge we measured. Final expense insurance covers those costs with a small whole life policy, usually $5,000 to $25,000, that pays cash directly to your family.

This is our home state. Senior Solutions Insurance works from Greenwood Village, and the licensed agent who calls you back sits in that office.
fe.observation: Colorado is cheaper than average on every measure. Cremation at $1,650 is 17% below the national median and burial at $2,565 is 8% below; the non-declinable basic services fee, $1,985, is 10% below. Colorado families generally need less coverage for the funeral home’s bill than the national averages suggest — the cemetery is where the number climbs.
fe.coverageNote: For a Colorado family choosing burial, the funeral home’s bill is below average but the cemetery’s is not, so the Front Range plot price tends to decide the total. Ten thousand dollars covers the simplest burial with room to spare; a full service with a viewing points toward $10,000 to $15,000.

medicare.countyNote: Colorado has 64 counties, and Medicare Advantage availability is decided county by county, not statewide. The plans filed for Denver County are not the same list as the plans filed for Mesa or Weld, so the first question is not “what is available in Colorado” but “what is available where I live.”

aca.intro: Colorado runs its own marketplace, Connect for Health Colorado, rather than using healthcare.gov, and Senior Solutions Insurance is certified with it. Colorado has also expanded Medicaid, so the application sorts households by income: below roughly 138% of the federal poverty level you are routed to Health First Colorado, the state’s Medicaid program; above it, premium tax credits apply to a marketplace plan.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Colorado?

The 2026 median from 31 Colorado funeral home price lists is $1,650 for a direct cremation and $2,565 for an immediate burial, both below the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800. Those are funeral-home charges only; the cemetery bills a plot, vault, opening and closing, and headstone separately, typically $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Is final expense insurance cheaper in Colorado?

No. Premiums are set by your age, gender, tobacco use and health, and a 65-year-old in Denver is quoted from the same tables as a 65-year-old in Atlanta. What differs in Colorado is what you are insuring against: funeral-home charges here run 8 to 17% below national, so the same $10,000 policy stretches further.
How much coverage do I need for a Colorado funeral?

Add the cemetery to the funeral home. An immediate burial at Colorado’s $2,565 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,565–$7,565; a full traditional funeral with a viewing lands at $8,415–$11,415. Most Colorado families land between $10,000 and $15,000 once medical bills and small debts are added.
Do I need a medical exam to qualify?

No. Final expense underwriting uses a short list of yes/no health questions, a prescription history check and a database review. Most applicants qualify for a level benefit plan with full coverage from day one; those who do not can take a guaranteed acceptance plan with a two-year waiting period.
Where is Senior Solutions Insurance located?
In Greenwood Village, Colorado, at 5775 DTC Blvd, Suite 250-S. The agent who calls you back works from that office and is licensed by the Colorado Division of Insurance.
medicare: Which Medicare Advantage plans are available in my part of Colorado?

It depends on your county. Colorado has 64 counties and each plan files the counties it serves, so the options in Denver County differ from those in Larimer, El Paso or on the Western Slope. A licensed agent compares the plans filed for your county; the Medicare Plan Finder at medicare.gov does the same by ZIP code.
Where can I get free, independent Medicare help in Colorado?

Colorado’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), run through the Colorado Division of Insurance, offers free counseling from trained counselors who do not sell insurance, at 1-888-696-7213. It is a good second opinion on anything an agent tells you, including us.
Do I have to be in Colorado to work with Senior Solutions Insurance?
No, but Colorado is where we are. Our office is in Greenwood Village and our agents are licensed here first. If you live in the state, the person who calls you back is local.
When can I enroll in a Medicare Advantage plan?

In the seven months around your 65th birthday, during the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7 each year, during the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period from January 1 to March 31 if you already have a plan, or during a Special Enrollment Period after a qualifying event such as moving to a new county.
aca: Do I buy a marketplace plan in Colorado through healthcare.gov?

No. Colorado runs its own exchange, Connect for Health Colorado, and that is where every subsidized individual and family plan in the state is sold. Senior Solutions Insurance is certified with Connect for Health Colorado and can enroll you there at no extra cost.
Has Colorado expanded Medicaid?

Yes. Adults with household income up to about 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Health First Colorado, the state’s Medicaid program, so there is no coverage gap in Colorado. The marketplace application routes you to Medicaid or to a subsidized plan based on income.
How does the premium tax credit work?

It is calculated from your household income and household size and applied directly to your monthly premium, so the price you see after the credit is what you pay. We check what you qualify for before you pick a plan.
What if I am turning 65 in Colorado?

Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the premium tax credit for a marketplace plan ends and Medicare becomes your primary coverage. The usual next step is a Medicare Advantage plan filed for your county; a licensed agent can walk you through the transition on the same call.

fe.intro: A direct cremation in Tennessee has a median cost of $2,348 — 18% above the national median of $1,995 — and an immediate burial $2,990, which is also above the national figure. That cuts against Tennessee’s reputation as a low-cost state for services. Final expense insurance covers those costs with a small whole life policy, usually $5,000 to $25,000, that pays cash directly to your family.
fe.observation: Tennessee runs above the national median on every funeral-home charge. Cremation at $2,348 is 18% above national, burial at $2,990 is 7% above, and the non-declinable basic services fee of $2,298 is 5% above. If you assumed a Tennessee funeral would be cheaper than average, the price lists say otherwise; plan the coverage amount accordingly.
fe.coverageNote: Because Tennessee’s funeral-home charges sit above national, a Tennessee family should not round down. An immediate burial with cemetery costs already approaches $8,000 at the top of the range; a full service with a viewing points toward $15,000 rather than $10,000.

medicare.countyNote: Tennessee has 95 counties, and Medicare Advantage availability is decided county by county, not statewide. The plans filed for Shelby County are a different list from the plans filed for Davidson, Knox or a rural county on the Cumberland Plateau, so the useful question is what is available at your address.

aca.intro: Tennessee is one of the ten states that has not expanded Medicaid, and its residents buy individual and family plans on the federal marketplace, healthcare.gov, rather than a state exchange. The first fact matters more than the second: it creates a coverage gap for some lower-income adults, and where you fall relative to the federal poverty level decides which program you should be applying to.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Tennessee?

From 26 Tennessee funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median is $2,348 for a direct cremation and $2,990 for an immediate burial. Both are above the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800. Cemetery costs — plot, vault, opening and closing, headstone — are billed separately and add $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Why is cremation more expensive in Tennessee than the national average?

The price lists do not say why, only that it is: Tennessee’s $2,348 median for direct cremation is 18% above the national $1,995, and the basic services fee of $2,298 is above national too. The practical point is that Tennessee is not the low-cost state for funerals that it is for some other services, so do not size a policy on the national average.
How much final expense coverage does a Tennessee family need?

An immediate burial at Tennessee’s $2,990 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,990–$7,990 before any service. A full traditional funeral with a viewing runs $8,415–$11,415 with the cemetery included. With medical bills and small debts added, $10,000 to $15,000 is where most Tennessee families land, and the higher figure is the safer one here.
Are final expense rates different in Tennessee?

No. Premiums are set by age, gender, tobacco use and health, not by state. The rate table on this page applies to a Tennessee applicant exactly as it applies to anyone else; what changes is how much coverage you need, which the Tennessee funeral figures above help you decide.
Can I qualify with a health condition?

Usually. Simplified issue asks a short list of yes/no health questions with no exam, and common conditions such as controlled diabetes or high blood pressure typically pass. If your history rules that out, guaranteed acceptance asks no health questions at all, costs more, and pays the full benefit after two years.
medicare: Are the same Medicare Advantage plans available across Tennessee?

No. Each plan files the counties it will serve, and Tennessee has 95 of them. Memphis, Nashville, Knoxville and the rural counties between them can each have a different list. A licensed agent compares the plans filed for your county specifically.
Where can Tennessee residents get free Medicare counseling?

Through Tennessee’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), operated by the Tennessee Department of Disability and Aging, at 1-877-801-0044. Counselors are trained, free and do not sell insurance, which makes them a good independent check on any agent’s advice.
I moved to Tennessee from another state. Can I change my plan?

Moving to a new county is a qualifying event that opens a Special Enrollment Period, because the plans available to you have changed. Tell the agent your move date; the window is limited, so it is worth acting on promptly.
What are the regular enrollment windows?

The Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, and the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period from January 1 to March 31 for people who already have a plan. Special Enrollment Periods cover events such as moving or losing other coverage.
aca: Where do Tennessee residents buy ACA coverage?

Through healthcare.gov, the federal marketplace. Tennessee does not run its own exchange. Every subsidized individual and family plan in the state is sold there, and a licensed agent can enroll you at no extra cost.
Has Tennessee expanded Medicaid?

No. Tennessee is one of ten non-expansion states as of medicaid.gov’s most recent reporting. Adults who do not fit a traditional Medicaid category and earn less than 100% of the federal poverty level fall into a coverage gap, because marketplace subsidies start at 100%. Above that line, premium tax credits apply.
How much will a Tennessee marketplace plan cost me?

It depends on your household income and size, because the premium tax credit is applied to the monthly premium before you pay it. The listed price is rarely the real price. We run the credit first, then compare plans on what you would actually pay.
I am turning 65 in Tennessee. Do I keep my marketplace plan?

Usually not. Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, your premium tax credit ends and Medicare becomes primary. The next step for most people is a Medicare Advantage plan filed for their Tennessee county.

Final expense insurance covers both with a small whole life policy, usually $5,000 to $25,000, that pays cash directly to your family.
fe.observation: Florida tracks the national median closely — cremation 6% below, burial 4% below, the basic services fee 8% below — so the national averages are a fair guide to the funeral home’s bill here. The figure they leave out is the cemetery: a plot, vault, opening and closing and a marker add $2,000–$5,000 or more, and in Florida’s larger metro cemeteries the upper end of that range is the realistic one.

Cremation with a memorial gathering can be covered comfortably by $10,000; burial with a service in a metro-area cemetery points toward $15,000.

aca.intro: Florida, with the largest share of seniors of any state, buys its individual and family plans on the federal marketplace, healthcare.gov, and has not expanded Medicaid. Both facts shape what a Florida household should do: everyone shops in the same federal exchange, but adults below the poverty level who do not fit a traditional Medicaid category fall into a coverage gap that expansion states do not have.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Florida?

From 32 Florida funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median direct cremation is $1,882 and the median immediate burial $2,695 — within a few percent of the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800. Those are funeral-home charges only; cemetery costs add $2,000–$5,000 or more on top.
Why do Florida funeral costs vary so much between quotes?

Because the cemetery is a separate business with a separate bill, and Florida plot prices vary widely between a metro cemetery and a rural one. The funeral home’s own charges in Florida are steady and close to national; the spread you see between quotes is mostly cemetery, casket and whether a viewing is included.
How much final expense coverage does a Florida family need?

An immediate burial at Florida’s $2,695 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,695–$7,695. A full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs lands at $8,415–$11,415. Add medical bills and small debts and most Florida families choose between $10,000 and $15,000.
Are final expense premiums higher for Florida residents?
No. Rates are set by age, gender, tobacco use and health, not by state or by hurricane exposure. The table on this page is the same one a Florida applicant is quoted from.
Can I buy final expense insurance in Florida if I spend part of the year elsewhere?

Yes. A final expense policy is not tied to a funeral home or a state; it pays cash to the person you name, wherever the funeral takes place. Tell the agent which state is your legal residence so the policy is issued correctly.
medicare: Does Florida have more Medicare Advantage plans than other states?

Florida has a large senior population and correspondingly many plans filed, but availability is still decided county by county across 67 counties. The number that matters is not how many plans exist in Florida; it is how many are filed for your county, and a licensed agent compares exactly that list.
Where can Florida residents get free Medicare counseling?

Florida’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program is called SHINE — Serving Health Insurance Needs of Elders — and is reachable at 1-800-963-5337. Counseling is free and independent; the counselors do not sell insurance.
I split the year between Florida and another state. Which plans can I use?

Medicare Advantage plans are tied to the county of your permanent residence, and many have service areas that do not follow you to a second home for routine care. If you spend months elsewhere, tell the agent; it changes which plan types are worth comparing.
When can I enroll or switch?

In the seven months around your 65th birthday, from October 15 to December 7 each year, from January 1 to March 31 if you already have a Medicare Advantage plan and want to make one change, or during a Special Enrollment Period after a qualifying event such as moving to a new county.
aca: Where do Florida residents buy ACA coverage?

Through healthcare.gov, the federal marketplace; Florida does not run its own exchange. Every subsidized individual and family plan in the state is sold there, and a licensed agent can enroll you at no extra cost.
Has Florida expanded Medicaid?

No. Florida is one of the ten non-expansion states in medicaid.gov’s most recent reporting. Adults outside the traditional Medicaid categories who earn less than 100% of the federal poverty level fall into a coverage gap; above 100%, premium tax credits apply to a marketplace plan.
What will I actually pay for a Florida marketplace plan?
The premium after your tax credit, which is set by household income and size and applied monthly rather than refunded at tax time. We calculate the credit first and compare plans on the net price.
I am turning 65 in Florida. What changes?

Your premium tax credit ends when Medicare Part A and Part B begin, and Medicare becomes your primary coverage. Most people then choose a Medicare Advantage plan filed for their Florida county; a licensed agent can handle both steps.

From 90 California funeral home price lists collected in 2026 — the largest sample of any state — the median direct cremation is $1,895 and the median immediate burial $2,499, both below the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800. Cemetery costs are separate and, in California’s coastal metros, often exceed the $2,000–$5,000 national range.
Why is a California funeral expensive if the funeral home is cheaper than average?

Because the funeral home is only half the bill. California’s funeral-home medians are 5 to 11% below national, but the cemetery — plot, vault, opening and closing, marker — is billed separately, and urban California plots are among the most expensive in the country. How much final expense coverage does a California family need?

An immediate burial at California’s $2,499 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,499–$7,499, and a full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs comes to $8,415–$11,415. The California Department of Insurance, which licenses agents and carriers and takes consumer complaints.

When are the enrollment windows?

The Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period from January 1 to March 31 for people already in a plan, and Special Enrollment Periods after qualifying events.
aca: Do Californians use healthcare.gov?

No. California runs its own exchange, Covered California, and that is where every subsidized individual and family plan in the state is sold. A licensed agent can help you enroll there at no extra cost.
Has California expanded Medicaid?

Yes. Adults with household income up to about 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medi-Cal, so California has no coverage gap. The Covered California application routes you to Medi-Cal or to a subsidized plan based on income.
Does Covered California run a longer open enrollment than healthcare.gov?

State-based marketplaces set their own windows, and Covered California’s has often run longer than the federal one. The dates are set each plan year, so we confirm the current window on the call rather than publishing one here.

Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the premium tax credit ends and Medicare becomes primary, so most people leave the marketplace plan. The usual next step is a Medicare Advantage plan filed for your California county.

medicaid.section: Georgia has not expanded Medicaid. Traditional adult Medicaid is limited to specific groups — children, pregnant women, some parents with very low income, people with disabilities and older adults. Georgia does run a limited alternative, Georgia Pathways to Coverage, for adults aged 19 to 64 with household income up to 100% of the federal poverty level who complete 80 hours a month of qualifying activities such as work, education or community service. Because marketplace premium tax credits begin at 100% of the poverty level, an adult below that line who does not qualify for Pathways or a traditional category is in a coverage gap. Expansion status per medicaid.gov; Pathways criteria per pathways.georgia.gov.

fe.intro: A direct cremation in Georgia has a median cost of $2,525 and an immediate burial $3,225 — 27% and 15% above the national medians, and among the highest in the South. That cuts against the assumption that Southern states are cheap. Final expense insurance covers those costs with a small whole life policy, usually $5,000 to $25,000, that pays cash directly to your family.
fe.observation: Georgia is the most expensive of the eleven states we cover on both measures. Cremation at $2,525 is 27% above the national median, burial at $3,225 is 15% above, and the non-declinable basic services fee of $2,578 is 17% above. Forty price lists sit behind those figures, so this is not a small-sample quirk. A Georgia family sizing a policy on national averages will come up short.
fe.coverageNote: Georgia families should size toward the top of each band. Burial with cemetery costs already exceeds $8,000 at the upper end before any service; a full traditional funeral with a viewing points to $15,000, and even cremation with a gathering is more comfortably covered by $10,000 here than in a below-average state.

medicare.countyNote: Georgia has 159 counties, second only to Texas, and Medicare Advantage availability is decided county by county, not statewide. The plans filed for Fulton and DeKalb counties are not the plans filed for the small counties of south Georgia, and with 159 lists in play a neighbor’s plan one county over may simply not be offered at your address.

aca.intro: Georgia runs its own marketplace, Georgia Access, rather than using healthcare.gov, and it is one of the states that has not expanded Medicaid. Georgia instead runs a limited program called Pathways to Coverage, with an income cap at the poverty level and a monthly activity requirement, so where a Georgia household falls relative to the federal poverty level decides which program applies.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Georgia?

From 40 Georgia funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median direct cremation is $2,525 and the median immediate burial $3,225 — 27% and 15% above the national medians of $1,995 and $2,800, and among the highest in the South. Cemetery costs are separate and add $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Are funerals really more expensive in Georgia than the national average?

Yes, on every funeral-home charge we measured. The basic services fee, which cannot be declined, has a Georgia median of $2,578 against a national $2,195. With 40 price lists behind the figures, Georgia is one of the better-sampled states, so the finding is solid rather than a small-sample artifact.
How much final expense coverage does a Georgia family need?

An immediate burial at Georgia’s $3,225 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $5,225–$8,225 — the highest simplest-burial total of the eleven states we cover. A full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs comes to $8,415–$11,415 or more here. Most Georgia families should be looking at $15,000 rather than $10,000 for burial.
Are final expense premiums higher in Georgia?

No. Premiums come from the same age, gender, tobacco and health tables everywhere. What Georgia changes is the coverage amount: with cremation at $2,525 and burial at $3,225, both well above national, the same $10,000 policy covers less of a Georgia funeral than it does elsewhere, which is why $15,000 is the more common recommendation here.
Who regulates final expense insurance in Georgia?
The Georgia Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner, which licenses agents and carriers and handles consumer complaints.
medicare: Why does Georgia’s county count matter for Medicare Advantage?

Because plans file by county and Georgia has 159 of them, more than any state except Texas. Metro Atlanta counties can each have a different list, and rural south Georgia counties often have much shorter ones. A licensed agent compares only the plans filed for your county.
Where can Georgians get free Medicare counseling?

From the Georgia State Health Insurance Assistance Program, run through the Georgia Division of Aging Services, at 1-866-552-4464. Counseling is free and independent; the counselors do not sell insurance.
I live in a rural Georgia county. Will I have options?

Possibly fewer than metro Atlanta, and in some counties very few. That is exactly why the county check comes first: if the list is short, a licensed agent can tell you what alternatives exist rather than leaving you to guess.
When can I enroll or switch?

In the seven months around your 65th birthday, from October 15 to December 7 each year, from January 1 to March 31 if you already have a plan and want to make one change, or during a Special Enrollment Period after a qualifying event such as a move.
aca: Where do Georgia residents buy marketplace coverage?
Through Georgia Access, the state’s own exchange, not healthcare.gov. Every subsidized individual and family plan in Georgia is sold there, and a licensed agent can help you enroll at no extra cost.
Has Georgia expanded Medicaid?

No. Georgia is one of ten non-expansion states in medicaid.gov’s most recent reporting. It runs a limited program, Georgia Pathways to Coverage, for adults aged 19 to 64 up to 100% of the federal poverty level who complete 80 hours a month of qualifying activities. Adults below the poverty level who do not qualify for Pathways or a traditional Medicaid category fall into a coverage gap, because marketplace subsidies begin at 100%.
Does Georgia Access run a longer open enrollment than healthcare.gov?

State-based marketplaces set their own windows, and they sometimes run longer than the federal one. Georgia Access’s dates are set each plan year, so we confirm the current window on the call rather than publishing one here.
I am turning 65 in Georgia. What happens to my Georgia Access plan?

Once Medicare Part A and Part B begin, the premium tax credit ends and Medicare becomes primary, so the Georgia Access plan should end when Medicare starts. The next step is usually a Medicare Advantage plan — and in Georgia the county you live in decides which plans are filed for you, with 159 counties producing very different lists.

descriptions.fe: Final expense insurance in Arizona. A direct cremation runs $1,240, second-lowest in the country, and an immediate burial $2,045. Call 1-888-957-3337.
descriptions.medicare: Medicare Advantage in Arizona is filed county by county across 15 counties. A licensed agent compares the plans for your county. Call 1-888-957-3337, TTY 711.
descriptions.aca: ACA plans in Arizona are sold on healthcare.gov, with AHCCCS Medicaid below 138% of the poverty level. Agents check your subsidy first. Call 1-888-957-3337.

fe.intro: A direct cremation in Arizona has a median cost of $1,240 and an immediate burial $2,045 — the second-lowest cremation cost in the country, 38% below the national median. Final expense insurance covers those costs with a small whole life policy, usually $5,000 to $25,000, that pays cash directly to your family.
fe.observation: Arizona is the cheapest of the eleven states we cover, by a wide margin. Cremation at $1,240 is 38% below the national median and second-lowest in the country, behind only Nevada at $1,190; burial at $2,045 is 27% below national and the basic services fee of $1,550 is 29% below. Retirees moving to Arizona from higher-cost states are often insuring against a bill that is smaller than they expect — at the funeral home. The cemetery still charges what it charges.
fe.coverageNote: Arizona’s low funeral-home charges mean $10,000 covers more here than almost anywhere: cremation with a memorial gathering with room to spare, and even a simple burial with cemetery costs at the lower end of the range. A full traditional funeral with a viewing still points toward $10,000 to $15,000 once the cemetery is included.

medicare.countyNote: Arizona has just 15 counties, and Medicare Advantage availability is still decided county by county, not statewide. Maricopa County, home to Phoenix and the largest retiree in-migration in the state, has a different list of filed plans from Pima, Yavapai or the rural counties, and a plan offered in one is not automatically offered in the next.

aca.intro: Arizona uses the federal marketplace, healthcare.gov, for individual and family plans, and it has expanded Medicaid, which in Arizona is run through AHCCCS. That means one place to shop and no coverage gap: below roughly 138% of the federal poverty level the application routes you to AHCCCS, and above it premium tax credits apply to a marketplace plan.

fe: How much does a funeral cost in Arizona?

From 29 Arizona funeral home price lists collected in 2026, the median direct cremation is $1,240 — 38% below the national median of $1,995 and the second-lowest in the country — and the median immediate burial is $2,045, 27% below the national $2,800. Cemetery costs are separate and add $2,000–$5,000 or more.
Why is cremation so inexpensive in Arizona?

The price lists show the result, not the reason: at $1,240, only Nevada ($1,190) is lower. Arizona’s non-declinable basic services fee, $1,550 against a national $2,195, is a big part of it, since that fee is inside every cremation and burial price.
How much final expense coverage does an Arizona family need?

An immediate burial at Arizona’s $2,045 median plus $2,000–$5,000 of cemetery costs is $4,045–$7,045, the lowest simplest-burial total of the eleven states we cover. A full traditional funeral with a viewing and cemetery costs comes to $8,415–$11,415. Most Arizona families are well served between $10,000 and $15,000, and cremation is comfortably within $10,000.
I moved to Arizona in retirement. Should I adjust my coverage?

Possibly downward at the funeral home, since Arizona’s charges are 27 to 38% below national, but not before checking the cemetery and any medical bills or debts the policy should also cover. A licensed agent can rework the number with you.
Are final expense rates lower in Arizona?
No. Rates are set by age, gender, tobacco use and health, not by state. What is lower in Arizona is the bill you are insuring against, which means a given policy amount goes further.
medicare: With only 15 counties, are Arizona Medicare Advantage options the same everywhere?

No. Fifteen counties is fewer lists than many states, but they are still separate lists. Maricopa, Pima and Yavapai counties each have plans filed specifically for them, and the rural counties can have far fewer. A licensed agent compares the plans filed for your county.
Where can Arizonans get free Medicare counseling?
From the Arizona State Health Insurance Assistance Program (SHIP), at azship.org or 1-800-432-4040. Counseling is free and independent; the counselors do not sell insurance.
I just moved to Arizona. Can I change my Medicare Advantage plan?

Yes. Moving to a new county is a qualifying event that opens a Special Enrollment Period, because the plans available to you have changed. Many Arizona retirees are in exactly this position; tell the agent your move date, since the window is limited.
When are the regular enrollment windows?

The Initial Enrollment Period around your 65th birthday, the Annual Enrollment Period from October 15 to December 7, and the Medicare Advantage Open Enrollment Period from January 1 to March 31 for people already in a plan. For the many people who move to Arizona in retirement, the move itself opens a Special Enrollment Period, so a new Arizona resident does not have to wait for the fall.
aca: Where do Arizona residents buy ACA coverage?

Through healthcare.gov, the federal marketplace; Arizona has no state exchange. The application checks AHCCCS eligibility first, then calculates the premium tax credit for a marketplace plan. A licensed agent can enroll you at no extra cost.
Has Arizona expanded Medicaid?

Yes. Adults with household income up to about 138% of the federal poverty level qualify for Medicaid through AHCCCS, so Arizona has no coverage gap. The healthcare.gov application routes you to AHCCCS or to a subsidized plan based on income.
I retired to Arizona before 65. What are my options until Medicare?

A marketplace plan through healthcare.gov with the premium tax credit applied to your monthly premium, sized to your household income. Many early retirees qualify for a larger credit than they expect once earned income stops; we calculate it before comparing plans.
I am turning 65 in Arizona. What changes?

Your premium tax credit ends when Medicare Part A and Part B begin, and Medicare becomes primary. Most people then choose a Medicare Advantage plan filed for their Arizona county, which a licensed agent can compare on the same call.
